extracted.intended_audience: trademark attorneys, applicants, and USPTO/TTAB practitioners preparing or examining concurrent use trademark applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for preparing and prosecuting a concurrent use application before the USPTO/Trademark Trial and Appeal Board (TTAB), including required statements, jurisdictional cut-offs, geographic and mode-of-use limitations, and notice/publication rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Must Assert Use in Commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: A basic requirement for any concurrent use application is that it must assert use in commerce of the mark sought to be registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trademark Act § 2(d) governs concurrent registrations. For an application based on § 1(a) (use), the applicant may seek concurrent use registration at filing or later. An intent‑to‑use application under § 1(b) may not be amended to seek concurrent use until use is effected (see 37 C.F.R. § 2.76 and § 2.88). Applications based solely on § 44 or § 66(a) are not subject to concurrent use proceedings unless a second basis of use in commerce under § 1(a) (or an allegation of use under § 1(b) filed prior to amendment) is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional Requirement — Date of First Use Prior to Cut‑Off
rubrics_metrics.description: A concurrent use application must allege use in commerce 'prior to (1) the earliest of the filing dates of the applications pending or of any registration issued under [the Trademark Act]; (2) July 5, 1947, …; or (3) July 5, 1947 …' (i.e., a cut‑off date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a jurisdictional requirement: if the asserted first use date is not prior to the cut‑off, the applicant is normally not entitled to concurrent registration and the examining attorney should refuse registration. Exceptions: (a) consent of the owner of the involved application/registration; or (b) a final court determination that applicant is entitled to concurrent use. Case law examples and TTAB decisions illuminate application of the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Must Meet Requirements Applicable to Non‑Restricted Application
rubrics_metrics.description: A concurrent use application must specify and contain all the elements required by the rules of practice in trademark cases for a non‑restricted application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must satisfy the same basic application requirements as any application (e.g., proper drawing, identification, specimen/use showing). A concurrent use registration will not be awarded where other non‑satisfaction exists (e.g., a designation that is generic in the unclaimed territory). Extent of actual use is immaterial so long as use is more than token; failure to use the mark shown in the drawing in commerce prior to the relevant filing date can be fatal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Must Identify Nature and Extent of Restriction Sought
rubrics_metrics.description: In every concurrent use application the applicant shall (i) state exceptions to the claim of exclusive use and (ii) specify, to the extent of the verifier’s knowledge, any concurrent use by others, the goods and areas in which each concurrent use exists, the periods of each use, and the goods and area for which the applicant desires registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement derives from Trademark Act § 1(a)(3)(D) and 37 C.F.R. § 2.42. The applicant’s statement of the area, goods/services, and (if applicable) mode of use for which registration is sought gives notice at publication and in any subsequent concurrent use proceeding of the scope of the registration sought; the statement setting forth concurrent lawful use by others gives notice of the applicant’s acknowledgement of others’ rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verified Statement Required Content (37 C.F.R. § 2.42(b) items 1–9)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must include a verified statement that indicates, to the extent of applicant’s knowledge, specific information about applicant’s use and concurrent users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items (paraphrased from § 2.42(b)): (1) geographic area in which applicant is using the mark (or members’/authorized users’ area for collective/certification marks); (2) applicant’s goods/services (or members’/authorized users’ goods/services or nature of collective membership); (3) the mode of use for which registration is sought; (4) concurrent users’ names and addresses; (5) registrations issued to or applications filed by concurrent users, if any; (6) geographic areas in which each concurrent user is using the mark; (7) concurrent users’ goods/services (or members’/authorized users’ goods/services); (8) mode of use by concurrent users; and (9) time periods of use by concurrent users. The statement functions as formal notice when the application is published and when a concurrent use proceeding is instituted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic Restrictions — Description and Scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Concurrent use registrations are normally geographically restricted; the application should specify the geographic area sought and any exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concurrent rights usually arise where parties in good faith adopt and use the same or similar mark in separate geographic areas. Prior users may seek registration covering the United States except for a subsequent user’s area of actual use (and possibly natural expansion); subsequent users often seek registration for area of actual use plus natural expansion. If another party owns an incontestable registration, the concurrent registration will be limited to the applicant’s area of actual use prior to actual/constructive notice unless parties stipulate otherwise. The geographic description should be sufficiently definite — if less than a state, use counties or other specific terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode of Use Restrictions — When They Support Concurrent Registration
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may in rare instances seek concurrent registration based solely on conditions or limitations as to the mode of use of its mark (or as to the goods/services or trade channels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mode of use refers to manner of displaying the mark (stylization, trade dress, house mark, disclaimers). Mode‑of‑use concurrent registrations typically arise from court determinations; the TTAB cannot allow concurrent registration if it finds likelihood of confusion. Applicant should seek concurrent registration on mode‑of‑use grounds only if the condition cannot be incorporated into the drawing/identification of the mark and cannot be incorporated into any conflicting application/registration; if incorporable, the matter should be presented as a regular application and conflicts addressed by opposition or cancellation to impose appropriate restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify Excepted Users and Their Asserted Rights (scope of duty to disclose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must state, to the extent of applicant’s knowledge, the concurrent lawful use of the mark by others, setting forth their names and addresses; areas of use; goods/services; mode of use; periods of use; and registrations or applications filed by them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant need not list every entity known to be using the same or similar mark. The duty is to list any entity known to be a senior user of a clearly conflicting mark and any junior user known to have clearly established rights (e.g., by court decree, settlement, or registration). Failure to specify areas or services of an excepted user may lead to denial. Applicants must amend declarations to acknowledge rights recognized by settlement agreements when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication, Notice, and Marking of Concurrent Use Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is determined to be registrable subject to a concurrent use proceeding, the mark will be published for opposition and notification of institution of any concurrent use proceeding will be sent to the applicant and excepted users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no oppositions are filed (or all are dismissed/withdrawn), the Board will send notice of institution of the concurrent use proceeding and include a web link/address to access Office records related to the proceeding. When approved for publication, the application is marked by the examining attorney with a statement such as: 'SUBJECT TO CONCURRENT USE PROCEEDING WITH ________________. APPLICANT CLAIMS EXCLUSIVE RIGHT TO USE THE MARK IN THE AREA COMPRISING ________________.' See 37 C.F.R. §§ 2.80, 2.99(c), 2.99(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility of §44 and §66(a) Applications for Concurrent Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications based solely on Trademark Act § 44 or § 66(a) are not subject to concurrent use registration proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application under § 44 may not seek concurrent registration unless it also includes a second basis for registration — an allegation of use in commerce under § 1(a) or, if based also on § 1(b), an allegation of use under 37 C.F.R. § 2.76 or § 2.88. A § 66(a) application may not claim more than one basis and is therefore never subject to concurrent use proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and Amendment Rules for Intent‑to‑Use Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An intent‑to‑use application under § 1(b) may not be amended to seek concurrent use until use is effected and an acceptable allegation of use has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent‑to‑use applicants seeking concurrent registration must first file an acceptable allegation of use under the applicable regulations (37 C.F.R. § 2.76 or § 2.88) before amending the application to seek concurrent use. Examining attorney practice and case law caution that applicants were previously advised they could not seek concurrent use until an acceptable allegation of use was on file.
